chapter.title: Python Using ooRexx
chapter.para: From Python, the bridge is the module oorexx: interpreters, Rexx objects, ADDRESS environments and Rexx's standard streams. showed how to run Rexx code; these recipes go further.

section.title: Rexx Objects in Python
section.para: You want to use Rexx objects from Python.

How it works. A Rexx object comes to Python as an oorexx.RexxObject: o.name(args) sends the message NAME, o[k] is Rexx's [], len(o) is items, and iterating it is DO OVER. Strings, numbers, .nil and Arrays are converted instead: an Array comes as a list, a copy, and a Rexx string that is a number, such as the 20261007 of standardDate, as a Python int, which str() makes text again.

section.title: An ADDRESS Environment in Python
section.para: You want Rexx programs to send commands to Python code.

How it works. A Python function of two arguments, the command and a context, is the environment: given to Interpreter in command_environments, or added later with add_command_environment, it is a command handler like those written in Rexx (ooRexx's .CommandHandler), and from Rexx .CommandHandler~register(name, .py~commandHandler(f)) does the same. What it returns is RC. The context is ooRexx's own .CommandContext: through it the function sets the variables of the code that issued the command (setVar), reads ADDRESS ... WITH INPUT lines (ctx.input()) and writes WITH OUTPUT ones (ctx.output()).

section.title: Rexx's Output in Python
section.para: You want to capture what Rexx code says, or to feed it input.

How it works. In an interpreter Python creates, Rexx's standard streams go through Python's sys.stdout, sys.stderr and sys.stdin, looked up at every line, so contextlib.redirect_stdout, a notebook or a log captures them. Each line is marked as BSF4ooRexx marks it, REXXout> or REXXerr>; prefixes=False leaves the marks out. A Rexx program started by rexx can do the same with call py.redirectTo.

section.title: Messages by Name
section.para: You want to send a message whose name is in a variable, or is not a Python name.

How it works. BSF4ooRexx's RexxProxy methods: sendMessage takes the name as a string and the arguments in a list, and sendMessage0 to sendMessage5 take them one by one. sendMessageScope starts the method search at a class, as Rexx's o~name:scope: here the superclass's describe.
